name: 4-Card Brag
description: 4-Card Brag is a strategic variation of standard 3-Card Brag. In this version, every player is dealt four cards and must choose the best three to form their Brag hand, discarding the fourth. This added step of hand selection significantly increases the average hand strength and reduces the luck element of the initial deal. Once the hands are set, play proceeds with the classic half-price blind betting and Brag hierarchies.

history.origins: 4-Card Brag developed as a popular regional variant in the UK, designed to provide more player agency than the strictly deterministic deal of 3-Card Brag. It is particularly common in casual pub games where players want slightly 'bigger' hands to play with.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Multi-card Brag variants gain popularity in British card clubs.
1980s: Standardized as a common Dealer's Choice option.
Present: A frequent favorite in online Brag communities.
history.cultural: Reflects the British preference for card games that allow for skill-based selection and tactical 'mucking'.
history.evolution: The game retains all the core 'Blind' and 'See' rules of its parent but adds a 'Pre-Vying' phase where hands are optimized.

setup.dealing: Deal four cards face-down to each player. Players choose three to keep and place the fourth face-down in a shared muck pile.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, betting chips or currency.

rules.objective: Win the pot by forming the best three-card hand from the four dealt, or by forcing others to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Selection**: Players receive 4 cards and discard 1. 2. **Vying**: Standard Brag betting follows. Players choose to play 'Blind' (without looking at their chosen 3) or 'See'. 3. **Ranks**: Prial > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: The choice of which three cards to keep is the only skill difference from 3-Card Brag.
Equal hands favor the player who remained Blind longer.

strategy.basic: Prioritize pairs and consecutive suits when choosing your three cards. A low pair is often better than three high unconnected cards.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Hidden' Kicker: If you have a choice of two identical pairs (e.g., two 8s and a 10 vs two 8s and a 4), always keep the highest kicker to win tie-breaking showdowns.
strategy.advanced: Discard Influence: Track which ranks are being mucked. If you see several players mucking 3s, the probability of someone holding a Prial of 3s (the top hand) drops significantly.
tips: Don't spend too long choosing; the core of the game is still the betting phase.
If you are dealt three of a kind in your four cards, keep them! It's an automatic Prial.

variations.name: 5-Card Brag
variations.description: Players receive five cards and choose three, leading to even stronger average hands.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine differences for 5-Card Brag are not yet modeled as overrides in this file.

scoring.winCondition: Last player standing or best three-card hand at showdown.

synthesis.shortDescription: A tactical variation of standard Brag that grants players more agency. Every player receives four cards and must choose the best three to take into battle. This selection phase deepens the strategy, leading to higher-ranked showdowns and more intense bluffing rounds.
